correctness.rationale: Every non-overlapping word is unbordered hence primitive, and two codewords from one rotation orbit would share a nonempty proper suffix/prefix. All weight-three imprimitive words are exactly the n/3 triple-repetitions when 3 divides n. This yields floor((n-1)(n-2)/6) primitive orbits. For each n>=4 the construction with 1s at (1,a,b), 2<=a<=floor((n+2)/3), a+1<=b<=n-floor((n+2)/3)+1 has no matching suffix/prefix: a suffix beginning at the second 1 has two 1s versus all three in the equally long prefix, while a suffix beginning at the third 1 has one versus at least two. Other suffixes begin with zero versus prefix one. The exact sum of constructions equals orbit upper bound for every residue mod 3; n=3 is empty. check.py checked all ordered overlaps and exhaustive primitive necklace coverage for each 3<=n<=30, but proof is analytic for all n.

originality.rationale: The exact binary fixed-weight-three all-length maximum and explicit primitive-necklace transversal are not entailed by the inspected Dyck, run-restricted, generalized alphabet, unrestricted-size, balanced, or non-expandability results. Index searches using the same concepts, aliases, formula and source identifiers yielded no direct covering finding. The primitive orbit upper bound is standard and by itself does not prove attainability; the attaining prefix/suffix-compatible code is the substantive new step. value.rationale: The natural weight-three synchronization capacity is fully determined at every length and an explicit maximum code is given. Constraining weight to three is a motivated sparse-frame constraint; the exact count is the full primitive necklace orbit bound, not just a minor finite improvement. Saturation of that bound requires the nontrivial simultaneous prefix/suffix compatibility established by the construction. The result can be used directly for enumerating and generating optimal sparse synchronization codebooks, without claiming error correction, uniqueness, or larger-weight generality.
